sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by Flag antibody immunofluorescence on live non-permeabilized HEK293T cells (L1). OR function not specifically measured for OR1E1 in this study.
sites.rationale: L3 explicitly states that the construct carries 'only an 8-amino acid Flag tag on the mature protein' at the N-terminus of the full-length OR, and L1 confirms OR1E1 surface detection by Flag antibody on live cells. OR1E1 has no signal peptide per the computed topology (residues 1-28 are extracellular), so the mature protein begins at residue 1 (M) and the tag prepends before it (insert_after_residue=0). The N-terminal extracellular span is 28 residues, placing the junction 28 residues from TM1 (residue 29), well above the ≥3-residue minimum. No specific residue number is named in the paper; the position is derived from the single extracellular terminus of this GPCR-type receptor. PMC3698168 tested 15 human ORs including OR1E1 in HEK293T cells using constructs carrying an 8-amino-acid Flag tag on the mature N-terminus of the full-length, membrane-anchored OR. Surface expression was assessed by Flag antibody labeling of live, non-permeabilized cells. OR1E1 was among the ORs detected at the cell surface.

sources.claim: In fact, two-thirds of Lucy-tagged ORs are able to reach the cell surface synergistically with chaperones even when the Rho tag is removed (10/15 ORs), allowing for the potential assessment of OR function with only an 8-amino acid Flag tag on the mature protein.

literature_notes: All three ledger lines derive from the same paper (PMC3698168), which tests a panel of 15 human ORs including OR1E1 with N-terminal Flag-tagged constructs in HEK293T cells. L3 is the most informative, specifying an 8 aa Flag tag on the mature N-terminus of the full-length OR. L1 confirms surface detection of Flag-tagged ORs by live-cell immunofluorescence. L2 describes the Lucy trafficking tag added to the N-terminus to boost surface expression; the Lucy tag is cleavable and is not itself the surface epitope tag. No ledger line names a specific residue number for the Flag insertion, and no internal loop insertions are reported for OR1E1 or any close ortholog in the ledger. The paper does not report OR1E1-specific functional data (e.g., cAMP or calcium response to odorant ligand), so validation_level is surface_only. The Lucy tag construct (L2) is a cleavable trafficking aid, not a permanent surface tag, and is not proposed as a separate site. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are named in the ledger.
